title: session reshuffle latency-cost atlas (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a set of microbenchmarks and early synthesis for a session-reshuffle approach: periodically redistributing warm session state across a GPU pool to reduce long-tail p99 latency during sustained surges. Focus: show latency tail vs cost (dollars/100k tokens) tradeoffs and surface quick heuristics for product teams.

Status:
- draft: exploratory lab runs on staging cluster (8xA100/2TB aggregate KV state).
- high-level takeaway (tl;dr): a conservative reshuffle (every 10–15m, thresholded on idle ratio) reduces p99 by ~15–25% during surge windows with a 2–6% increase in amortized $/token; aggressive reshuffle every 1m reduces p99 by ~40% but increases $/token by 10–18% due to extra KV warm transfers.

Methodology (quick):
- workload: sessionized chat emulator, mix modeled on traffic capture (70% short chats < 60 tokens, 20% medium 60–300 tokens, 10% long > 300 tokens). Burst profile: background 400 qps -> ramp to 4k qps over 60s, hold 5m, decay 2m.
- baseline config: pinned-session affinity (sessions stay on same GPU), autoscale to cap, KV cache prewarm on session creation; no reshuffle.
- reshuffle variants: 
  1) periodic-10m: pick coldest 10% of GPUs every 10m, move session blocks to balance slot fill.
  2) thresholded-15m: reshuffle only if idle-slot-ratio > 0.35 and pending-requests > 0.2*capacity.
  3) aggressive-1m: reshuffle candidate hot sessions every 1m to coalesce active sessions on fewer GPUs.
- metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 generation latency (ms), tail spike count (events > 2x p99 baseline), token-throughput sustained, and amortized dollars per 100k tokens (est. infra + data transfer + additional warmup cost).
- runs: 5 repeats each; numbers below are median across repeats.

Experiment matrix (abbreviated):
- cluster: 8xA100 80GB (simulated multi-tenant load).
- model: open-llama-13B quantized path used in staging.

Results (key slices):
1) Latency summary (median of runs):

Scenario       | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tail events
---------------|----------|----------|----------|----------|-----------
baseline        | 84       | 158      | 212      | 420      | 38       
periodic-10m    | 86       | 150      | 198      | 358      | 22       
thresholded-15m | 85       | 147      | 192      | 330      | 15       
aggressive-1m   | 92       | 132      | 176      | 255      | 6        

Notes: p99 reductions vs baseline: periodic-10m ~14.8%, thresholded-15m ~21.4%, aggressive-1m ~39.3%. Tail event counts fall proportionally.

2) Cost estimate (amortized $/100k tokens) - simplified approximation used for quick tradeoffs:
- baseline: $0.82 / 100k tokens (steady-state, includes KV warm fraction ~3%).
- periodic-10m: $0.86 / 100k (+4.9%) — extra KV transfer overhead and slightly lower packing efficiency during reshuffle window.
- thresholded-15m: $0.85 / 100k (+3.7%).
- aggressive-1m: $0.97 / 100k (+18.3%).

ASCII chart: p99 vs cost (normalized to baseline = 1.0 cost, 1.0 p99)

Label         | p99_norm | cost_norm
--------------|----------|----------
baseline       | 1.00     | 1.00    
periodic-10m   | 0.85     | 1.05    
thresholded-15m| 0.79     | 1.04    
aggressive-1m  | 0.61     | 1.18    

Quick visual (bar-like):
p99 reduction (higher left shorter right):
baseline       [##########] 1.00
periodic-10m   [########  ] 0.85
thresholded-15m[#######   ] 0.79
aggressive-1m  [###       ] 0.61

cost hit (bars):
baseline       [##########] 1.00
periodic-10m   [###########] 1.05
thresholded-15m[###########] 1.04
aggressive-1m  [##############] 1.18

Interpretation / tradeoff framing:
- Conservative reshuffle (periodic-10m / thresholded-15m) gives a favorable p99 improvement with modest cost impact. For many customer SLAs (p99 target reductions of 15–25%) this looks like a strong candidate.
- Aggressive reshuffle aggressively reduces p99 but the incremental dollar cost is material; recommend reserving aggressive mode for premium SLA tiers or transient incidents.
- The thresholded variant often beats blind periodic because it avoids unnecessary transfers when the cluster is already well-packed.

Failure modes observed (lab):
- flash-transfer storms: simultaneous reshuffle across >50% nodes caused transient KV bus saturation -> short-lived p50 spikes (seen in agressive-1m runs when no backoff).
- packing oscillation: naive reshuffle heuristics cause flip-flopping (sessions moved repeatedly between two hosts) — requires move damping/TTL.

Open questions / TODOs:
- refine cost model: current estimate lumps inter-node network and GPU warm cycles into simple percent; need instrumented run with real billing simulation (linked ticket JIRA-RT-1048).
- fairness: does reshuffle increase variance across tenants? run multi-tenant fairness sweep (TODO: include tenant-A/B/C mix).
- prefetch policy: can we gate moves on predicted session revisit probability using the session predictor? small accuracy gains could avoid many moves.
- safety: implement global reshuffle window limiter to avoid >20% concurrent moves.

Suggested next steps:
1) Prod-proxy trial: apply thresholded-15m on a single low-risk region for 72h with monitoring alarms for transfer rate and p50/p99 regressions (owner: Marcus Liu).
2) Add move damping and per-session move TTL to prevent thrash.
3) Wire an instrumentation flag to measure exact additional GPU-seconds used by reshuffle to refine $ estimate.
4) Run fairness multi-tenant runs with two customer profiles and measure tail cross-impact.

Appendix: micro-observations
- reshuffle is most effective for session mixes with high cold-to-hot churn (e.g., streaming chat apps where sessions see short bursts then idle).
- for long-lived sessions with heavy KV use, aggressive moves can add >200ms per move on average due to KV checkpointing; in those cases prefer thresholded with predictor.
